subject.title: [Bug]: OpenClaw Tool Lifecycle / Gateway Recovery Field Report

question: For replay-unsafe post-tool continuation failures, should OpenClaw preserve and resume the session from committed tool results, expose receipt-only diagnostics, or keep the current fail-closed warning until a narrower retry policy lands?
rationale: Current code intentionally avoids blind retries after possible side effects; changing that behavior requires a product/runtime decision about what state is durable enough to resume safely.

options.title: Define session-survival recovery
options.body: Persist enough post-tool state to resume or quarantine the failed continuation without asking users to reconstruct side effects manually.

options.title: Ship receipt-only diagnostics
options.body: Expose richer tool lifecycle receipts and failure reasons while leaving resume/retry behavior unchanged, which improves debugging but keeps manual recovery burden.

options.title: Defer to replay-policy work
options.body: Treat this field report as context for the narrower replay-unsafe incomplete-turn policy issue and avoid separate recovery semantics for now.

recommendation.title: Define session-survival recovery
recommendation.body: Persist enough post-tool state to resume or quarantine the failed continuation without asking users to reconstruct side effects manually.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses agent runner safety and product recovery semantics, and steipete appears in adjacent terminal-classifier/replay history plus current area ownership signals.
